notes: H2 is the C2 redaction fixture. AMENDED 2026-09-02 by Vaibhav's decision: NAMES ARE KEPT, only contact details are removed. Thirteen values must not survive into storage - eight email addresses and five phone numbers. EVERY OCCURRENCE COUNTS, not the first. The eight forms of four external contact names that this file previously required to be redacted are now in expected_retentions and MUST SURVIVE. That is a specification change, not a relabelled failure: external-name redaction was built and worked (BUG-009), and was withdrawn because a requirement is only reviewable if you can tell who asked for it - a speaker whose role is never stated is identified by nothing but their name, so redacting it orphans the requirement rather than anonymising it. WHAT MUST SURVIVE, and why it is written down at all: expected_retentions carries external names, internal stakeholder names (Dana, Marcus, Priya, Tom), customer organisations (Northwind Logistics, Meridian Bank, Halcyon Retail Group and their short forms) and job titles. Before this amendment the file listed only what must GO, so a redactor that removed every capitalised word would have scored 21 of 21 and passed the 100% floor cleanly - over-redaction was structurally invisible to this dataset. C2 now fails on a retention that goes missing, which makes 'PII redaction quietly starts eating the document' a red case instead of a silent change of policy. CUSTOMER ORGANISATION NAMES stay, unchanged from the original reading: 'Northwind needs SSO' is the requirement and redacting the company would gut the corpus. LABELS ARE WRITTEN AGAINST THE PRE-REDACTION TEXT, because that is what this fixture is: the document as it arrives at the door. All five requirement and open-question quotes were chosen to contain no redactable value, so each survives redaction byte-identical and still resolves by substring search against the stored raw_text. Redaction shifts character offsets; it does not disturb these spans.
